title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Guess: elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni and Ti blended in equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) ratio
recollection.intervention: Guess: high-energy mechanical alloying (several hours of planetary ball milling under argon) followed by consolidation through spark plasma sintering at a range of temperatures (≈900–1100 °C) and short holding times
recollection.structure: Guess: nanocrystalline single-phase solid solution (predominantly FCC with some BCC or L12 nanoprecipitates) with grain size <100 nm, nearly full density (>99 %) and occasional Ti-rich oxide or intermetallic dispersoids
recollection.mechanism: Guess: severe plastic deformation during milling produces solid-solution supersaturation; rapid Joule-heating and pulsed current in SPS promote diffusion-controlled densification while suppressing grain growth, yielding an ultra-fine structure responsible for high hardness; grain-growth kinetics analyzed by an Arrhenius model giving a relatively high activation energy because of sluggish diffusion in the HEA
recollection.results: Guess: Vickers hardness on polished samples about 10-12 GPa (≈1000–1200 HV); relative density 98–99 %; grain-growth exponent n≈4 and activation energy Q≈160–200 kJ mol⁻¹ derived from isothermal holds; compression or nanoindentation tests indicate yield strength >2 GPa with limited ductility.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies argon-atmosphere high-energy milling followed by short, high-temperature SPS, and captures the nanocrystalline, predominantly FCC/mixed FCC-BCC structure. Its strengthening explanation—milling-induced deformation/supersaturation plus SPS densification and grain-growth suppression—is substantially correct, though some proposed phases and kinetic details are speculative. The numerical results are substantially wrong: actual hardness was 675 HV, yield stress 1238 MPa, compressive strength 1894 MPa, grain size <48 nm, and phase fractions 83% FCC/17% BCC.
